source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 5: vector with zero dot product with i, j, k (book p.275). Answer agrees with the key (PDF 312).

blocks.prompt: 5. If \(\underline{v}\) is a vector for which \(\underline{v}\cdot\underline{i} = 0\), \(\underline{v}\cdot\underline{j} = 0\), \(\underline{v}\cdot\underline{k} = 0\), find \(\underline{v}\).
blocks.explanation:
Each dot product with a unit vector picks out one component of \(\underline{v}\).
We must find \(\underline{v}\).
Plan: write \(\underline{v} = a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\), take the three dot products, and read off \(a\), \(b\), \(c\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{v}\cdot\underline{i} = 0\), \(\underline{v}\cdot\underline{j} = 0\), \(\underline{v}\cdot\underline{k} = 0\).
To find: \(\underline{v}\).
Method: Let \(\underline{v} = a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\); use \(\underline{i}\cdot\underline{i} = 1\), \(\underline{i}\cdot\underline{j} = 0\), etc. (14.2.2).

Dot with \(\underline{i}\)
\[\underline{v}\cdot\underline{i} = a(1) + b(0) + c(0) = a\]
\[a = 0\]
Why: \(\underline{i} = 1\underline{i} + 0\underline{j} + 0\underline{k}\), so only the \(\underline{i}\) component survives.

Dot with \(\underline{j}\) and with \(\underline{k}\)
\[\underline{v}\cdot\underline{j} = b = 0\]
\[\underline{v}\cdot\underline{k} = c = 0\]
Why: In the same way each unit vector picks out its own component.

Write \(\underline{v}\)
\[\underline{v} = 0\underline{i} + 0\underline{j} + 0\underline{k} = \underline{0}\]
Why: All three components are zero.

Check
\[\underline{0}\cdot\underline{i} = \underline{0}\cdot\underline{j} = \underline{0}\cdot\underline{k} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The zero vector is perpendicular to every vector (Note in 14.2.6). No non-zero vector can be perpendicular to all three axes at once.
